why.Home Lake and Constance Pass, reaching D: When already camped at Home Lake for a neighbouring peak, or when linking into a longer high route or loop, this reaches the same basin from the south instead of via Royal Basin.

review.notes: Royal Basin is the usual way; Constance Pass appears in loop and linkup reports.

wa_mount_noyes_standard.primary: Low Divide and Seattle Basin to the Noyes–Meany col

why.Elwha River to Low Divide: When coming in from the north side or linking the peak into a long cross-range traverse; it is far longer than reaching Low Divide from the Quinault side.

review.notes: Both ways reach Low Divide; the Quinault route is shorter and the stored notes say the peak is normally tagged from a camp near the divide. Primary choice is moderate confidence.
Hoh trail is the only walk in. The second entry is the upper glacier line, and reports say most summit teams choose Crystal Pass.

problems: The second 'way in' is the upper-mountain route from Glacier Meadows, not an alternative approach; reports say most parties use Crystal Pass, so it may deserve to be modelled as part of the route rather than a way in.
why withdrawn in review: the second entry reads as the standard upper route, not an alternative approach — settle pass

why.From the Heather Lake trailhead when the: In winter and shoulder seasons when the forest road is closed to vehicles below the normal trailhead, forcing a long extra walk up the road.

review.notes: Winter gate closure confirmed; adds roughly 5 miles and 1,300 ft.

why.Silver Creek from Ross Lake: When staying entirely within the United States, avoiding the foot crossing of the border and the rough road to Depot Creek, at the cost of a boat ride and a long bushwhack.

review.notes: Depot Creek is described as the easier route; Silver Creek is a seldom-used bushwhack via the Ross Lake water taxi.

problems: The marked primary (Depot Creek) crosses the border on foot away from a port of entry, which is unlawful; the lawful all-US way (Silver Creek) is not marked primary. Owner decision needed; mark not changed.

why.Comet Falls and Van Trump Park: Late in the season, when the Nisqually Glacier is broken and rockfall-prone; this starts lower and runs longer but never crosses it, and the trail stays free of snow far up.

review.notes: Paradise is the usual start; Comet Falls is the late-season alternative.

wa_mount_rainier_kautz_headwall.primary: Paradise and Glacier Vista, across the Nisqually to the Turtle and Camp Hazard

why.Comet Falls and Van Trump Park: Late in the season, to avoid crossing the Nisqually Glacier and to have water low down; it starts far lower, and the descent through the trees is easy to lose.

review.notes: Sources call the Paradise start with the Nisqually crossing the most common; Comet Falls is the longer alternative.

why.Mowich Lake and Spray Park: In early summer once its road is open, for a shorter walk in, if a car shuttle to the White River end can be arranged, since the usual descent comes out there.

review.notes: Reports say the Mowich start is shorter but needs a shuttle and its road opens late; many current parties use White River and descend the Emmons. The Mowich road is now closed to the public per stored note.

problems: Stored Mowich notes call it the start most parties would choose, which conflicts with White River being marked primary; reports lean toward White River now, so the mark looks right but the note should be softened.

why.Up the Elwha to Low Divide: When coming from the north side or crossing the range on foot; it takes several days, so most parties prefer the shorter Quinault walk to Low Divide.

review.notes: Low Divide is reached from either river; the Elwha approach is much longer.
fromStoredNotes: Up the Elwha to Low Divide

why.Fisher Chimneys and Winnie's Slide, then: For parties who would rather use the maintained Lake Ann trail and a known camp than the White Salmon valley bushwhack, accepting a climb then a loss of about a thousand feet.

review.notes: Searches confirm Fisher Chimneys then White Salmon Glacier is a used approach to the north side; no head-to-head comparison found.

why.Mount Baker Ski Area (Chair 8) traverse: In winter or spring on skis, when the road walk and clearcut are unattractive; start at the ski area and traverse down into the White Salmon valley.

review.notes: Search did not confirm Chair 8 specifically; reason taken from stored notes and ski reports.

why.Up the White Salmon valley to the lower: For parties who prefer a longer valley walk and a glacier approach to the crest over the brushy creek crossing and ridge climb of the other line.

review.notes: The ridge-opposite-ski-area line is the one the route description recommends; the valley option is documented as the alternative.
